stories.headline: Pentagon Signs AI Deals With 8 Firms for Classified Networks; Anthropic Still Blacklisted

key_facts.fact: SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, Reflection AI, Microsoft, and AWS signed agreements to deploy frontier AI on the Pentagon's Impact Level 6 and 7 classified networks for 'lawful operational use'
key_facts.excerpt: The War Department has entered into agreements with seven of the world's leading frontier artificial intelligence companies, SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services to deploy their advanced AI capabilities on the Department's classified networks for lawful operational use.

key_facts.fact: Oracle separately agreed to join the roster, bringing the total to eight companies
key_facts.excerpt: On Friday, the Pentagon posted on the social media site X that Oracle Corp. had also joined the roster of technology companies that had agreed to deploy their AI tools on classified networks.

key_facts.fact: GenAI.mil, the Pentagon's AI platform, has been used by over 1.3 million personnel, generating tens of millions of prompts and deploying hundreds of thousands of agents in just five months
key_facts.excerpt: Over 1.3 million Department personnel have used the platform, generating tens of millions of prompts and deploying hundreds of thousands of agents in only five months.

key_facts.fact: Pentagon CTO Emil Michael said Anthropic remains designated a supply chain risk and its Claude models are barred from use by defense contractors
key_facts.excerpt: Defense Department CTO Emil Michael on Friday said Anthropic is still a supply chain risk... defense contractors have to certify that they do not use Anthropic's Claude models in their work with the military.

key_facts.fact: Michael called Anthropic's Mythos model a 'separate national security moment' due to its capabilities for finding and patching cyber vulnerabilities
key_facts.excerpt: The Mythos issue that's being dealt with government wide, not just at Department War, is a separate national security moment where we have to make sure that our networks are hardened up, because that model has capabilities that are particular to finding cyber vulnerabilities and patching them.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic sued the Trump administration in March to try to reverse the Pentagon's blacklisting
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic sued the Trump administration in March to try to reverse the Pentagon's blacklisting.

stories.headline: Musk Testifies xAI 'Partly' Used OpenAI Models to Train Grok via Distillation

key_facts.fact: During cross-examination on April 30 in Oakland federal court, Musk was asked if xAI distilled OpenAI's technology and said 'Partly'
key_facts.excerpt: Asked on the stand whether he knew what model distillation was, Musk said it's to use one AI model to train another. When asked whether xAI has distilled OpenAI's technology, Musk seemed to avoid the question... And when asked if that was a yes, he said, 'Partly.'

key_facts.fact: Musk described distillation as standard industry practice, saying 'It is standard practice to use other AIs to validate your AI'
key_facts.excerpt: When pressed, Musk said, 'It is standard practice to use other AIs to validate your AI.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's terms of service prohibit outputs from being used to train competing AI models
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's terms of service prohibit outputs from being used to train competing AI models.

key_facts.fact: Musk ranked current AI providers: Anthropic #1, OpenAI #2, Google #3, Chinese open-source #4, characterizing xAI as much smaller with just a few hundred employees
key_facts.excerpt: Musk was asked about a claim he made last summer that xAI would soon be far beyond any company besides Google. In response, he ranked the world's leading AI providers, saying Anthropic held the top spot, followed by OpenAI, Google, and Chinese open source models. He characterized xAI as a much smaller company with just a few hundred employees.

key_facts.fact: The admission is notable because OpenAI and Anthropic have accused Chinese firms including DeepSeek of using distillation, but this is a rare public acknowledgment from a US-based lab
key_facts.excerpt: That conversation has focused on Chinese firms using distillation to create open-weight models that are nearly as capable as U.S. offerings... Now we know it's true in at least one case.

stories.headline: Huawei Expects AI Chip Revenue to Hit ~$12B in 2026, Up 60%, as Ascend Orders Surge

key_facts.fact: Huawei expects AI chip revenue to reach approximately $12 billion in 2026, up from $7.5 billion in 2025 — a jump of at least 60% — based on orders already received
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei expects revenue from its AI chips to reach approximately $12 billion this year, up from $7.5 billion in 2025, a jump of at least 60% based on orders already secured, the Financial Times reported.

key_facts.fact: The majority of 2026 orders are for the Ascend 950PR processor, which entered mass production in March, with an upgraded Ascend 950DT planned for Q4
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei received majority of orders this year for its latest Ascend processor 950PR, which entered mass production in March, and the firm plans to launch an upgraded version of 950DT in the fourth quarter.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's V4 model, released April 24 and optimized for Huawei Ascend chips, triggered a wave of procurement from Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent
key_facts.excerpt: The revenue surge has been supercharged by DeepSeek's release of its V4 AI model on April 24, which was specifically optimised to run on Huawei's Ascend chips. The move triggered a wave of procurement activity across China's largest technology companies, with Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent among those racing to secure supply.

key_facts.fact: Huawei plans to ship approximately 750,000 Ascend units in 2026, with full-scale shipments ramping in H2
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei plans to ship approximately 750,000 units in 2026, with full-scale shipments ramping in the second half of the year.

key_facts.fact: TrendForce forecasts the Chinese high-end AI chip market will grow 60%+ in 2026, with domestic chips potentially capturing around half the market
key_facts.excerpt: Analysts at TrendForce forecast the Chinese high-end AI chip market will grow by more than 60% in 2026, with domestically produced chips potentially capturing around half of that market.

key_facts.fact: Huawei is positioning the 950PR specifically for AI inference rather than training, betting on the faster-growing segment of AI compute demand
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei is not trying to beat Nvidia at training giant AI models. It is positioning the 950PR specifically for AI inference — the computation that happens when a deployed AI model generates a response to your query.

stories.headline: Nebius Acquires 20-Person Inference Startup Eigen AI for $643M to Boost Token Factory

key_facts.fact: Nebius agreed to acquire Eigen AI for approximately $643 million in stock and cash, valuing the 20-person startup at roughly $32 million per employee
key_facts.excerpt: Nebius Group, the Dutch cloud computing company that split from Russian internet provider Yandex in 2024, has agreed to acquire Eigen AI for approximately $643 million in stock and cash... $643 million for 20 people requires explanation. The explanation is inference.

key_facts.fact: Eigen AI specializes in maximizing the number of tokens each Nvidia GPU can generate during AI inference, using techniques like activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ)
key_facts.excerpt: Eigen AI's technology maximises the number of tokens... that each Nvidia chip can generate when running AI models. The technique that made Eigen AI's founders notable in the field is activation-aware weight quantisation.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder Wei-Chen Wang received the MLSys 2024 Best Paper Award for AWQ, now the standard for 4-bit model serving in production; co-founder Ryan Wang's SpAtten is the most-cited HPCA paper since 2020
key_facts.excerpt: Wei-Chen received the MLSys 2024 Best Paper Award for Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) quantization — now the standard for 4-bit model serving in production deployments... Ryan's pioneering Sparse Attention (SpAtten) work is the most-cited HPCA paper since 2020.

key_facts.fact: Eigen AI's inference optimization layers will be integrated into Nebius Token Factory, its managed inference platform, which already ranked among the fastest on Artificial Analysis
key_facts.excerpt: The two companies have already delivered jointly optimized implementations of leading open source models that ranked among the fastest on Artificial Analysis.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition establishes Nebius's Bay Area engineering and research presence; the founding team includes MIT HAN Lab and CSAIL alumni
key_facts.excerpt: Nebius highlighted that it was acquiring 'elite inference research talent'... European AI infrastructure company Nebius has acquired a US startup which specialises in improving the performance of leading open-source AI models.

key_facts.fact: Inference is forecast to account for roughly two-thirds of AI compute demands in 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Inference is the fastest growing part of AI and is forecast to account for around two-thirds of compute demands this year.

stories.headline: Google Rolls Out Gemini to Cars With Google Built-in, Replacing Google Assistant

key_facts.fact: Gemini is rolling out as a software update to both new and existing cars with Google built-in, starting with English in the US, replacing Google Assistant
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini — your helpful AI assistant — is starting to roll out in cars with Google built-in as an upgrade from Google Assistant... The rollout will start with English in the United States and continue over the coming months.

key_facts.fact: Cars with Google built-in first hit the road in 2020; the update covers existing vehicles, not just new ones
key_facts.excerpt: When cars with Google built-in first hit the road in 2020, we made a commitment that your car will get better over time. That means that Gemini is coming not only to new cars, but also to existing ones through a software update.

key_facts.fact: Gemini integrates with manufacturer-provided owner's manuals to answer vehicle-specific questions like how to prepare for a car wash or adjust trunk height
key_facts.excerpt: On cars with Google built-in, Gemini can access manufacturer-provided owner's manuals to answer specific questions about car models.

key_facts.fact: GM previously announced Gemini is coming to approximately 4 million vehicles from model year 2022 and newer across Cadillac, Chevrolet, Buick, and GMC
key_facts.excerpt: General Motors revealed yesterday that Gemini is coming to approximately 4 million vehicles from model year 2022 and newer, spanning brands like Cadillac, Chevrolet, Buick, and GMC.

key_facts.fact: Features include Gemini Live for free-flowing conversations while driving, Google Maps integration for contextual stop recommendations, and message summarization
key_facts.excerpt: Drivers and passengers have the option to enter Gemini Live, similar to the Android experience... Gemini will reference information from Google Maps to find options, then you can follow up with questions.
